# Al-Faris AlZakwani's portfolio through a recruiter's eyes

**Independent review · 21 November 2026 · Repository revision `02fac28`**

## Executive assessment

The portfolio makes the astronaut ambition memorable. It makes the reader work to discover what Al-Faris can contribute today. Its strongest professional story is already demonstrable: a physics undergraduate at Sultan Qaboos University who builds web interfaces, has made a thermal-energy concept interactive, and contributed front-end work to a student proposal about astronaut health. That is a credible path from physics through software toward space technology.

**The biggest missed opportunity is Solvex.** The card sends a recruiter to the startup homepage. One level deeper, the reviewer could change solar intensity and see the simulated temperature difference and power output respond. That interaction explains the relationship between physics and software better than the four preparation pillars above it. A second missed opportunity is NexCore. Its public repository describes a released bilingual student platform, while the portfolio describes a studio in general terms. [Solvex simulator](https://faris-zak.github.io/SOLVEX/tile.html) · [NexCore project README](https://github.com/NexCore-Labs-Initiative/NexCore/blob/main/README.md)

**Overall score: 5.6/10 for professional presentation.** The evidence warrants a closer look for a student front-end opportunity. A space-industry or academic reviewer has a reason to start a conversation, but little basis yet to judge engineering or research depth. An improvement in evidence selection would matter more than a visual redesign.

## Strengths worth preserving

- **The journal has a recognizable author.** The portrait, Oman origin, restrained cyan and amber accents, and recurring field-note typography give the site a personality. The mobile view stacks cleanly in the sampled state. Full-width body text is generally easier to read than the small instrument-style labels.
- **Several descriptions already make defensible distinctions.** Solvex is a former role. AI Family Corp is being established. The club positions are nominations. UTAS participation includes the non-win. The Artemis boarding pass is explicitly symbolic, and the conference account says Al-Faris asked a question. Preserve those distinctions when shortening the prose.
- **There is evidence of service as well as ambition.** Teaching HTML and CSS at SQU, presenting astronomy to children over two days and completing 20 hours of Esnad workshops are specific, understandable activities. These examples carry more weight than a standalone leadership adjective.
- **There are working routes for readers who know what they want.** Work and Contact have direct anchors, the contact area offers email alongside its form, and the archive has keyboard dismissal and focus return. The code includes a skip link, focus styles, reduced-motion handling and a performance control. These features are worth retaining through any editorial changes.

## Verified findings

“Verified” describes the evidence in the second column. Recruiter impact and priority are reviewer judgments. P0 means a blocker across the main journey, P1 a significant credibility or evaluation problem, P2 a meaningful improvement for one task, and P3 optional polish. Estimates are hands-on effort for one person with access to the material. Waiting for an issuer, teammate or new research result adds elapsed time. No P0 was established.

## Editorial judgments and proposed wording

These priorities reflect the three audiences in the brief. They can be tested with a short reading task before restructuring the page.

| ID and location | Evidence and judgment | Consequence and suggested change | Priority · effort · confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| J1 · Hero, field note, Selected Work footer, Contact. `index.html:117–132`, `:516–520`, `:658–662` | The opening motto ends in a double period. The journal later explains its own metaphor. Contact invites collaborations, engineering opportunities, product ideas and general conversation together. | These lines spend scarce attention without making a specific invitation. Remove the repeated explanation. Use one long-term sentence and name the kinds of conversations welcome now, subject to actual availability. | P1 · 1–2 h · high |
| J2 · Work B, E, G and the Novacare feature. `index.html:419`, `:456`, `:483`, `:501` | A venture in formation appears before a deployed business site. “CEO” describes a title; the NexCore repository describes a product and release. Solvex and VitalX each connect two of the stated disciplines. | Keep My Portfolio first and compact. Give the next prominent slots or links to Solvex, NexCore and VitalX. Move the family venture to a short work-in-progress entry unless there is a deliverable to show. | P1 · 2–4 h for hierarchy · high |
| J3 · Hero effects, Trajectory console and roadmap. `index.html:140–181`, `:249–319`, `script.js:909–939` | The orbital portrait adds identity. The five interactive trajectory controls select a highlight among five related cards; the prose also lists most of those subjects elsewhere. The mono labels work for metadata and are comparatively small for primary navigation. | Preserve the portrait and color system. Consolidate duplicated text first. Keep a control if it leads to a concrete example. Test a slightly larger nav label and reduced decorative movement around sustained reading. | P3 · 2–4 h · medium |

**Hero draft**  
“I'm Al-Faris AlZakwani, a physics undergraduate at Sultan Qaboos University in Oman. I build web interfaces, including a thermal-energy simulator for Solvex, and contributed front-end development to VitalX, a student proposal for astronaut health monitoring. I want to apply physics and software to space technology.”  
Primary action: **Explore my projects**. Secondary action after a suitable file exists: **View my CV**. The full formal name can remain in the page title, biography and CV.

**Solvex draft**  
“As a software engineer on an SQU student startup, I built a 3D simulation for its agricultural tile concept. Adjust the solar intensity to see how the model's temperature difference and estimated power change. I later left the team.” Action: **Try the tile simulation**. Add the model assumptions or implementation detail only after confirming them.

**VitalX draft**  
“At the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, I contributed front-end development to VitalX, Team Novacare's proposal for astronaut health monitoring. I received the Galactic Problem Solver participation certificate.” Follow this with a named feature and one screenshot or team-approved submission when available. [LinkedIn About](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfarismujahid/)

**UTAS draft**  
“On 28 June 2026, I participated in the UTAS Summer Challenge at the Ibra branch. Our platform team proposed a way to support students from entry through graduation. We did not win.” The certificate substantiates participation, venue and date. The team description and result come from the portfolio.

| Project | What the reader can substantiate now | What deserves space |
|---|---|---|
| My Portfolio | The live site itself, responsive navigation, generated CV entry point and HTML/CSS/JS implementation. | Keep first. Replace the tour of the site's contents with one design or engineering decision readers can verify here. |
| AI Family Corp | The site describes a family venture being established. | A short status entry. Add the first actual deliverable if and when available. |
| AlDuwiki Cement Products | Its destination exposes products, approvals, location, contact and an Arabic-language control. The portfolio attributes the website to Al-Faris. | Lead client example. Explain what the client needed and which parts Al-Faris delivered. A visitor being able to locate products and contact the company is already a concrete outcome. Lead or sales figures would require records. [Company site](https://alduwiki-cp.com/) |
| Scorleaf | An Arabic-language site for a student startup, with product and team information. | The contribution is web development. Emphasize the interface, audience and delivered work. Attribute the health concept to the startup and avoid using therapeutic effectiveness as evidence of software success. [Startup site](https://faris-zak.github.io/Scorleaf/) |
| Solvex | The destination names the team and provides a working simulation with environmental inputs and telemetry. | Strongest current physics/software demonstration. Deep-link it and explain one model limitation. Preserve former-role status. [Company site](https://faris-zak.github.io/SOLVEX/) · [Simulation](https://faris-zak.github.io/SOLVEX/tile.html) |
| MindSync | A public repo exists. Its README describes it only as an education website and links a license. | Link one student task with a screenshot or demo and identify the implementation contribution. A bare repository link would still leave the purpose unclear. [MindSync README](https://github.com/faris-zak/MindSync/blob/main/README.md) |
| NexCore Labs | Its README identifies a bilingual community platform, Project Hub, contributor tools and a tagged release. It distinguishes active features from work in development. | Strong software case. Describe one release and the author's own contribution. The platform's scope is documented. Individual ownership of each feature needs attribution. [NexCore README and release links](https://github.com/NexCore-Labs-Initiative/NexCore/blob/main/README.md) |
| Space Research Initiative | A named LEO debris topic and an explicitly early stage of independent study. | Keep under independent study until there is inspectable work. A narrow question about orbital decay, with assumptions, a plot and a short interpretation, would be sufficient in principle. |
| VitalX / Team Novacare | LinkedIn supplies the name and intended use. The portfolio's certificate image documents participation. | Promote from event coverage to a team-project brief. A proposal, prototype and deployed system represent different outcomes. Use the one the artifact supports. |

## Professional credibility and LinkedIn

The exact LinkedIn profile linked in Contact was read in the available signed-in session. Its headline, About and Featured sections provide a useful comparison. Both sites are the author's accounts. Agreement establishes consistency, not independent verification of delivery. [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfarismujahid/)

| Claim | Comparison and disposition |
|---|---|
| Identity and education | Name, SQU physics, front-end development and interest in space technology align. LinkedIn leads with the present degree and mentions a **formally planned** computer science minor. Preserve “planned” if this is added to the portfolio. Confirm any expected graduation date directly before publishing it. |
| Leadership and ventures | LinkedIn describes founding NexCore as an online student initiative. The site uses CEO of a student-driven studio. Both may be true, but “founder of a bilingual student platform” conveys scope more clearly. The SQU nominations and former Solvex role are explicitly qualified on the site. |
| Conference and hackathons | LinkedIn Featured points to the same Middle East Space Conference video and describes asking a question. Both profiles describe a contribution to Team Novacare. The certificate photograph calls it participation and names the team. The official 2026 event dates agree. A team submission or a demo would substantiate the work separately. [Official Space Apps event](https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/) |
| Awards and credentials | The archive's 24 entries support “20+ certificates & learning milestones” as worded. Attendance, course completion, presenting a workshop, a language result and winning a competition carry different meanings. The three early awards lack enough identifying detail in the timeline to verify their scope. The UTAS original resolves the date and venue discrepancy. |
| Public proof | The conference link supports a recorded exchange, the festival event link supplies event context, and a guest passport documents public engagement. None demonstrates an institutional appointment or a completed research investigation. The site already acknowledges the symbolic nature of the boarding pass and the absence of affiliation. |

## Recruiter stress test

These are simulated screening judgments about what the page communicates. They are not interviews with employers.

| Perspective | First impression and strongest evidence | Weakest area, missing information and reason to hesitate | Improvement most likely to change the decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Software engineering recruiter** | A student who cares about front-end craft and has shipped beyond a personal site. AlDuwiki is easy to inspect. NexCore's release and the working Solvex controls are stronger engineering signals once found. | The cards list technologies and titles but rarely expose a specific change, constraint, test or ownership boundary. MindSync's README adds little. I would explore a junior front-end conversation, but cannot yet tell which complex feature Al-Faris could independently deliver. | Put NexCore or the SQU refactor behind one evidence link with a release or before/after, explain exactly what he changed, and add a working demo and a dated outcome. |
| **Aerospace / space-industry recruiter** | The interest is sustained over multiple activities. The best evidence of transferable ability is modeling an input and displaying telemetry at Solvex. VitalX gives the software work a space-related use case. The rocketry workshop adds relevant exposure. | The candidate-style panel and large campaign artifacts appear earlier than either technical example. Solar and thermal outputs show a software model; its assumptions, validation and individual scope remain unclear. There is no public evidence here of flight hardware, operational deployment or a formal astronaut programme. | Present the model as a learning or concept simulation, document its limits, and give VitalX a separate team brief. Specify a realistic student contribution such as front-end tooling for scientific data if that matches the opportunity sought. |
| **Academic research supervisor** | The BSc, waves/interferometry interest and astronomy teaching suggest curiosity and communication ability. The LEO study gives a plausible starting topic. | I can see what the student follows and explains. I cannot inspect how they formulate a question, choose a method, check a result or respond to uncertainty. The site gives no clear request for supervision or research availability. | Feature one short study note with references, calculation or notebook, result and limitations. Name relevant completed coursework and the type of supervised work sought once confirmed. |

## Scores and overall assessment

Equal-weight 10-point scale. **5** means a patient reader can make a partial judgment, **7** means a first-time reader can reach relevant proof with little effort, and **9** means the main claims are immediately clear and independently inspectable. Scores assess the public presentation and its links.

| Category | Score | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Content | 6/10 | Specific client, teaching and volunteer examples, with candid status language. The issuer omissions, UTAS discrepancy and repeated mission language weaken otherwise credible detail. |
| Professional identity | 5/10 | Strong recall for astronaut ambition. Current undergraduate status, software output and a plausible near-term contribution are much clearer on LinkedIn than in the hero. |
| UX/UI | 7/10 | Cohesive visual system, working sampled navigation, responsive stacking and keyboard archive behavior. The mobile portrait, visually ambiguous menu and unmarked project links make the search for evidence slower. |
| Project presentation | 5/10 | Shipped sites and an interactive simulator exist. Three direct destinations among eight cards, few technical decisions and limited ownership detail make comparison difficult. |
| Recruiter effectiveness | 5/10 | A motivated software reviewer can assemble a case. Aerospace and academic reviewers must do most of the synthesis. The public CV workflow also drops project links. |
| **Overall** | **5.6/10** | **28 points across five categories.** The most valuable change is making the strongest existing work easy to inspect, then filling the genuine gap in research evidence. |

**Review limits.** Desktop and mobile were rendered in the in-app browser, with mobile simulated by viewport. All in-page href fragments resolved, and all 24 distinct relative `src`/`href` paths from the HTML existed in the checkout. All three project destinations returned meaningful content through the browser or web reader. No external link was classified as broken solely because a reader could not fetch it. Video playback, anonymous Drive access, live contact delivery, print/PDF output, hardware accuracy, assistive-technology speech output and cold-network performance were not verified. Observations about loading come from assets and source behavior. Research authorship and business outcomes were not independently authenticated.
